chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Arthur Lyons revealed to be Russian
summary: A fight between Lyons's brother Sam and a Greek busboy exposes in Russian that Lyons was Russian.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Way later, see. So, anyhow, how I come to find out that Lyons was Russian. Because he talked very -- he was clever and he talked very good English. But we come to find out that he'd gone with Zukor and all those other guys.

So anyhow, he had a brother Sam Lyons, Sam Lyons got in an argument with the busboy. And they started fighting. Well, the busboy was Greek and Sam was Russian. So when they started fighting, they forgot their English altogether. One started talking in Greek and the other one started talking in Russian. And I still wouldn't have known, but one of the waiters, one of the white waiters, we had white waiters, see. He said, 'This is a funny argument. Here's one cursing one out in Greek and the other one in Russian.' I said, 'Who's speaking Russian?' He said, 'Sam, Sam Lyons's is a Russian.' And the busboy was Greek. So then, when Arthur said to me, Arthur Lyons wasn't his name. He had a name like Reboski, or something like that, see?
So, when he was surprised that when I told him that he was Russian, he said, 'How did you know that?' I said, 'Your brother told me.'
He got in this fight and he told us that.
